See [terminal operation and verification](../tui/run-and-test.md) for client startup, keys and validation. The commands below manage the independent Core; exiting TUI does not stop Core.

Run from the repository root with Node.js ≥22.19, npm, Python 3 and the pinned Pi submodule. World uses the journal; PostgreSQL provides log search and one-time legacy import.

## Installation, startup, and shutdown

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
npm ci
npm start
npm run core -- status
npm run core -- attach
npm run stop
```

The defaults are the fixture model and `.demo-data` directory. `start` launches background Core or connects to an existing instance. `status` and `attach` read an existing instance and exit 1 if none exists; `stop` exits 0 if none exists. [core-cli](../../src/pi_secretary/src/core-cli.ts) manages lifecycle only; use [CoreClient](../../src/pi_secretary/src/core-client.ts) or [API v1](api/v1/README.md) for domain operations.

`SECRETARY_DATA` selects the directory; administration commands must use the same directory and `SECRETARY_MODE`. `core-endpoint.json` stores the address, instance, and local token; `core.log` stores logs. Both have mode 0600. Background Core keeps running when clients close.

## Live models and database

The [start-live](../../src/pi_secretary/scripts/start-live.ts) wrapper reads separate main/task keys from credential JSON and always uses the deepseek provider:

```sh
npm run start:live
SECRETARY_MODE=live SECRETARY_DATA=.demo-data/interactive-live npm run core -- status
SECRETARY_MODE=live SECRETARY_DATA=.demo-data/interactive-live npm run stop
```

The wrapper defaults to credentials in `.demo-data/deepseek-credentials.json`, data in `.demo-data/interactive-live`, main model deepseek-flash, and task model deepseek-flash. Role-model environment variables override model names. Direct `SECRETARY_MODE=live npm start` uses role settings from the environment and permits other providers.

After upgrading, manually configured `opencode` and `opencode-go` providers fail in live mode with `RETIRED_LIVE_PROVIDER`. For the wrapper, configure official DeepSeek credentials in `.demo-data/deepseek-credentials.json`. The old `.demo-data/live-credentials.json` and OpenCode keys are retired. The next wrapper start of an existing `.demo-data/interactive-live` domain defaults both Main and Task to `deepseek-flash`.

| Environment variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| SECRETARY_DATA / SECRETARY_MODE | Data directory and fixture/live mode |
| SECRETARY_CREDENTIALS_FILE / SECRETARY_RUNTIME_FILE | Wrapper credential file / runtime configuration |
| SECRETARY_MAIN_PROVIDER / SECRETARY_TASK_PROVIDER | Role providers when starting Core directly |
| SECRETARY_MAIN_MODEL / SECRETARY_TASK_MODEL | Role models |
| SECRETARY_MAIN_API_KEY / SECRETARY_TASK_API_KEY | Role credentials |
| SECRETARY_PROVIDER / SECRETARY_MODEL | Shared defaults for direct Core startup |
| SECRETARY_DATABASE_URL | Log-search and legacy-import PostgreSQL DSN |
| SECRETARY_MAX_WORKERS | Concurrent executor limit, default 2 |

The live directory optionally reads `.demo-data/live-runtime.json`; `database_url` supplies a DSN, overridden by the environment. With `local_postgres_data` and no environment DSN, the wrapper starts the existing cluster using pg_ctl. The mem-only schema initializes at startup; `admin/world/migrate` retries initialization/import.Core stop closes connections while PostgreSQL stays running. Budget settings: [Memory and prompts](memory-and-prompts.md#Capacity and configuration).

## Common administration tasks

Every POST includes a UUID request_id. Retries of the same intent retain the original ID, path, and body. Reconcile 202 receipts through `requests/{id}`; related resources provide domain progress.

| Area | API path, prefix `/api/v1` |
| --- | --- |
| Conversation and recovery | POST messages, session/resume; GET timeline, requests/{id} |
| Work scopes | GET/POST scopes; POST scopes/{id}, scopes/{id}/archive |
| Tasks and decisions | POST task-requests, decisions/{id}/answer; GET tasks/{id}, executions/{id} |
| Approvals and rules | POST authorizations/{id}/decision; GET authorization-rules; POST admin/authorization-rules/{id}/disable |
| Settings | GET settings; POST settings/draft, settings/apply, settings/applications/{id}/retry or restore-draft |
| Memory | POST session/compact, memory/extraction/retry, memory/commitments/{id}/resolve |
| Unknown effects | POST operations/{id}/verify-write or operations/{id}/resolve |
| Reminders and push delivery | GET wakeups; POST wakeups/{id}/cancel; see the [dedicated guide](api/v1/push.md) for push configuration |
| Programs and database | POST admin/programs, admin/world/migrate |

DIRECTORY uses an existing physical root. Creation/updates check conflicts with other active roots, Core data, and still-occupied old roots. NONE only groups tasks; each uses its own directory. `default_write=ask` disables the built-in default write policy; active user rules still participate in matching. Archiving a Scope preserves history and slot-occupying executions and stops accepting new work.

This example registers the repository’s synthetic program with an existing Core:

```sh
SECRETARY_DATA=.demo-data node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'JS'
import path from 'node:path';
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { attachCore } from './src/pi_secretary/src/core-client.ts';
const client = await attachCore(path.resolve(process.env.SECRETARY_DATA));
if (!client) throw Error('Core 未运行');
console.log(await client.command('admin/programs', {
  request_id: randomUUID(), name: 'Synthetic report generator',
  entrypoint: path.resolve('src/pi_secretary/examples/report.mjs'),
}));
console.log(await client.query('admin/programs'));
JS
```

## Backup and upgrades

Stop Core and back up the full data directory, associated PostgreSQL database, code, and configuration. The data directory includes journal.jsonl, objects/, and workspaces/. Back up external DIRECTORY task roots separately. After shutdown, verify CAS read-only:

```sh
npx tsx src/pi_secretary/scripts/verify-cas.ts DATA_DIRECTORY
```

Verify replay on an isolated copy before switching directories. Recover unfinished Settings with the original configuration and check program paths and Execution bindings when moving directories. After the first World record or new prompt snapshot, old binaries cannot replay the journal: use a forward fix. Never overwrite newer writes with an older backup.Storage implementation: [Architecture](architecture.md#Data and commits).

Quit the TUI before backup and save its state directory together with Core data. The default is `~/Library/Application Support/Secretary/tui/v1/<domain>/`; custom launchers use their actual `stateRoot` (`data/tui` for agile). Preserve the entire directory, including unsent requests, original request_id values and recovery material, not only rebuildable caches.

## Troubleshooting

| Status | Action |
| --- | --- |
| OWNER_BUSY | Connect to or stop the existing Core for that directory |
| CORE_MODE_MISMATCH / UNSAFE_ENDPOINT | Check directory, mode, discovery-file ownership, and permissions |
| CAPACITY_BLOCKED / INPUT_EXIT_DISABLED | Check memory status, model budget, and PostgreSQL search watermark; restore the index, then retry maintenance |
| RECOVERY_BLOCKED | Check the checkpoint, call, and tool receipts in the recovery error, then use session/resume |
| RESULT_UNKNOWN | Verify the file write or resolve the effect from actual evidence; finalize after confirming controlled-process termination |
| Settings BLOCKED | Retry Settings with the exact compatible runtime; World facts have no SQL receipt bridge |
| RESYNC_REQUIRED | Obtain a new sync watermark, load resources, then catch up changes; reconcile original commands by request_id |
| SECRET_UNAVAILABLE / Push FAILED | Check private target configuration or stable error codes and inspect dispatch attempt records |
| journal/CAS corruption or append acknowledgment failure | Preserve a full copy and locate the recovery error; reopen and reconcile committed results against the journal |

## Development checks

```sh
npm run verify
SECRETARY_TEST_DATABASE_URL='<专用测试 DSN>' npm run verify
npm run docs:generate
npm run types:generate
npm run api:generate
```

verify runs type checks, link checks for Git-tracked Markdown, and `test_case/offline/**/*.test.ts`, in that order. The database role needs CREATEDB. The [test helper](../../test_case/offline/helpers/postgres.ts) creates and cleans up a separate `secretary_test_` database per scenario; missing local DSNs are explicitly skipped. `npm run test:db:clean` lists leftover databases; add `-- --apply` to remove candidates owned by the current role, with no active connections and a matching prefix.

[CI](../../.github/workflows/verify.yml) runs full verify with PostgreSQL 18 on Linux, and process recovery, push, Store ownership, and pipe tests on macOS. Aggregate verify requires both to pass. Track new documents in Git before docs:check; review checks section anchors and meaning. Inspect diffs after generation commands. See [online](test_case/online/README.md) for live-model tests and private configuration requirements, and [validation records](../api/v1/verification.md) for historical results.

## Current limitations

- Current entry points are Core CLI/API. The SwiftUI direction has been retired and client source removed; the [historical implementation](https://github.com/ExplodeCode6324/Secretary/blob/468a9c37939bb721792f353ea4970222a0bf58f2/src/secretary_macos/README.md) can be recovered from Git.
- Real phone delivery belongs to portable terminal #11; acceptance of actual macOS presentation awaits a later client phase.

Image attachments reserve capacity in a separate import ledger and bind immutable CAS to Inputs; see the [attachment guide](api/v1/attachments.md) for formats, budgets, residency and withdrawal.

## Guidance during execution

Core provides a durable Guidance API targeting an exact execution_id; see the [API guidance contract](api/v1/README.md#exact-execution-guidance-103) for usage and limits. Main can adjust execution through `task_control(action=guide, id=execution_id, task_id, text)`; this cannot approve authorization or answer Master-only questions.

Assess durable acceptance, checkpoint receipt and actual ModelCall adoption separately. Queued guidance cannot be silently dropped and must have a valid disposition before success; conflicts create explicit questions. New guidance does not undo started external effects or replay operations with unknown outcomes. After failure reconcile the original request identity and execution, never the next round. Ordinary Task input supports `/guide <exact title> <execution round> <body>`; authorization and questions still use the existing matter interface.

### Issue #106 isolated real-model acceptance

The acceptance-only launcher is [issue106-acceptance.ts](../../test_case/online/issue106-acceptance.ts). It creates an owned PostgreSQL cluster, World projection, loopback Core, separate rehearsal/Master draft roots and private command scripts under `.demo-data/issue106/acceptance/`. It never inherits `SECRETARY_*` production settings. Both roles use the existing checked private DeepSeek credential file; secrets are not copied into arguments, evidence or child environment.

The shared fsynced ledger counts physical provider attempts and proposed tools across roles and restarts (100 / 300). Preparation has its own two-hour wall-clock deadline. ARMED_FOR_MASTER keeps HTTP/SSE available with business pumping off. Only the first explicit Master connect starts the two-hour manual deadline; sleep counts. ACTIVE automatically resumes pumping after Core restart until the actual budget/deadline is exhausted. Reconnect never resets limits or requires the initial 60-attempt/180-tool reserve. EXHAUSTED retains history access. Budget extensions require explicit authorization and an atomic extension event; the launcher has no automatic reset.

Use the generated absolute commands in the handoff record. `prepare-task.command` creates a fresh directory scope with writes requiring approval, waits for a genuine model-generated pending authorization, and preserves prior scenarios. Native Terminal and Master's acceptance remain separate from automated HTTP/headless evidence.

The v4 legacy exporter intentionally rejects guidance-bearing state, including an accepted tombstone. Preserve/export the guidance evidence and use a **separate older-client state directory** for rollback; never point an older client at the v4 directory or delete the accepted binding to force export. Keep the original directory for returning to this version.

The [acceptance handoff](../fix/evidence/issue106-guide/handoff.md) documents explicit stop → authorized offline extension → start, private socket-directory recovery after long inactivity, and intentionally resubmitting revised guidance. Never edit a live in-memory budget ledger from outside its owner.
